entry.title: EvoGrain Uses L-Systems and Granular Synthesis for Algorithmic Sound Design
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | nathanho.me | discussion

EvoGrain is a rule-based system that generates audio using Lindenmayer systems (L-systems) and granular synthesis. The system utilizes an L-system to create command sequences for a "turtle" interpreter, which produces sets of grains defined by parameters such as pitch, duration, and amplitude. These grain sets are then synthesized into audio buffers ranging from a few seconds to 30 seconds in length.

Designed to produce raw material for sampling rather than complete musical compositions, EvoGrain employs an evolutionary optimization process to select the most musically interesting results. The architecture features a custom granular synthesis engine with phase modulation capabilities and a feedback delay network (FDN) reverb, using statistical analysis to guide the selection of optimal L-system rules.
